metadata.source: U.S. Census Bureau ACS 5-Year Data Profiles & Morris County 2026 Certified Rolls

zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Indian Lake & Rock Ridge Section, Downtown Broadway Village Core
keyFindings: Certified composite property tax rate is 2.584%, with an equalization ratio of 83.2%.
Public education represents 65.4% of property taxes, while municipal operations account for 24.8%.
Average residential assessment is $557,440, producing an average annual tax bill of $14,404.25.

neighborhoods.name: Indian Lake & Rock Ridge Section
neighborhoods.character: Famous 'Hub of Morris County' lake community with private beaches, community clubhouses, rustic ranches, and colonials
neighborhoods.description: Idyllic lake community featuring 4 recreational lakes, scenic boat docks, and lake association summer events.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Lake maintenance assessments and municipal flood control bonding on the Rockaway River.

neighborhoods.name: Downtown Broadway Village Core
neighborhoods.character: Vibrant pedestrian downtown with artisan bakeries, boutiques, Denville NJ Transit train station, and walk-to-town homes
neighborhoods.description: Charming town square featuring destination dining and direct commuter rail connections on the Morristown and Montclair-Boonton lines.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Commercial downtown ratables and Saint Clare's Hospital complex support municipal revenues.

equityAnalysis.summary: Denville Township maintains a certified residential tax roll across its neighborhoods.

keyTakeaways.title: Property Tax Burden & Household Income
keyTakeaways.detail: In Denville Township, homeowners pay an average of $14,404.25 annually in property taxes, consuming approximately 9.19% of median household income.

keyTakeaways.title: Equalization Ratio & Revaluation Balance
keyTakeaways.detail: With an equalization ratio of 83.2%, assessed values average ~83.2% of current true market values, establishing the basis for certified county tax equalization.

keyTakeaways.title: School District vs Municipal Levy Split
keyTakeaways.detail: Local education represents 65.4% of the total tax bill, municipal government absorbs 24.8%, and Morris County claims 9.8%.
